# opencode-usage-pace **What OpenCode costs, and when your Go allowance runs out — in the TUI, next to your session.** `ccusage`-style usage for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai): a sidebar block that separates what the catalog _would_ charge from what OpenCode Console _actually_ billed, and a full-screen page with the daily burn curve, the projected allowance-exhaustion day, a per-model table and a per-session cache breakdown. ``` Usage · list ← every provider, catalog prices, this machine today 8.4M tok · $3.74 7 days 139M tok · $36.78 30 days 450M tok · $115.31 cache 44.0B read · 83.7K write 14 days ▁▂▄▅▃▆▇█▅▃▂▄▆▅ Billed ← OpenCode Console, what was charged 24h $1.78 · 250.5M tok 7 days $9.20 · 1.8B tok 30 days $47.77 · 7.8B tok cache 98.7% of input · 246.7M 14 days ▃▄▆▇█·▂▃▄▆▇█·▂ Go rolling 15% · 100% in 2h weekly 50% · Oct 28 monthly 3% · Nov 24 details › ```
Full page (/ccusage) ``` opencode / ccusage 1 [24h] 2 7d 3 30d Billed · OpenCode Console · 24h $2.47 · 1,010 requests · in 3.2M · out 642.9K · cache 246.7M read / 0 write cache explains 98.7% of input tokens Burn · $0.98 of $6.00 · proj $2.62 · +$0.08/day · ~160% by reset · out ~Nov 2 · 20 days left $3.00┤ ┊ ┤ ┊ ░░░░ ┤ ┊ ░░░░░░░░░ ┤ ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ $1.50┤ ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ ┤ █████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ ┤ ██████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ $0.00┤████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ Oct 14 Nov 14 Models · 24h model req in out cache r cache w cost deepseek-v4.1-flash 912 2.4M 572.4K 235.7M 0 $1.32 Go allowance rolling 15% of the 5-hour allowance · reaches it in 2h · resets Oct 26 weekly 50% of the weekly allowance · resets Oct 28 monthly 3% of the monthly allowance · resets Nov 24 This session · 42 steps · $0.50 charged tokens cost share input 1K $0.01 1.9% output 250 $0.01 1.9% cache read 500K $0.47 93.9% cache write 1K $0.01 2.3% 1 24h · 2 7d · 3 30d · esc or q back ```
Status: early, single-author, and it reads two **undocumented** Console endpoints (see [Limits](#limits)). Every number it prints is either read from a file on your machine or fetched from an endpoint listed below — nothing is estimated without being labelled as such. ## Install Requires OpenCode v2 (`opencode --version` → 2.x, whose plugins come from `@opencode/plugin/tui`). ```bash opencode plugin add @lenucksi/opencode-usage-pace ``` Releases go through npm's staged publishing: a version is submitted to the staging queue and only becomes installable once a maintainer approves it with 2FA. Until then the package page shows nothing but the `0.0.0-stage` placeholder. Restart OpenCode. To configure by hand instead, add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "plugins": ["@lenucksi/opencode-usage-pace"], } ``` For hacking on it, clone and point the plugin directory at the checkout — plugins are also discovered from `~/.config/opencode/plugins//` and need no config entry: ```bash git clone https://github.com/lenucksi/opencode-usage-pace ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-usage-pace ``` Pick **one** of the two: a clone and an npm install of the same plugin load it twice, which duplicates the sidebar block and the command-palette entry. ### What you need - **For the local block:** nothing. It reads the session database OpenCode already writes. - **For the billed block, the burn chart and the Go meters:** a sign-in to OpenCode Console (or an OpenCode Go subscription), done once with `/connect`. The plugin reads that workspace credential from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (`integration = opencode`, `active = 1`, type `oauth`). An API key is not enough — Console answers allowance questions per workspace, and a key carries no workspace. ## Using it | | | | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Sidebar | Three blocks, each folds on click; the folded heading keeps the headline number | | `details ›` | Opens the full page (also: `/ccusage`, or the palette entry “Usage and billing”) | | `1` `2` `3` | Switch the billed range on the page (chips are clickable too) | | `esc` `q` | Back to where you came from | ## How the numbers are made Two money columns, deliberately apart: - **Usage · list** — `session.stats` over the local database: tokens and cost for _every_ provider you use, priced from each model's catalog rates. This is what the tokens _would_ cost at list price. - **Billed** — `/api/usage/summary` and `/api/usage/cost-by-day` from the Console: the amount actually charged, with cache reads and writes counted separately, and the same per-model table the Console web UI pages ten rows at a time. They disagree, and that disagreement is the point: on a Go subscription the catalog says $115 for a month that bills $48. Showing only one of them hides either your real spend or your real token appetite. **Pace.** The three Go meters are shares of their own allowances — a 5-hour window capped at 20% of your monthly limit, a week at 50%, a month at 100%. The plugin samples each meter on every refresh (persisted, capped at 120 samples) and projects the current slope: `100% in 2h`. A projection needs a baseline older than five minutes, is discarded when the window's reset changes underneath it, and is never shown if the limit would land _after_ the reset that clears it. Only a pace that lands within the day outranks the percentage colour. **Burn chart.** Cumulative billed spend for the current billing month, drawn from the daily series. Missing days are filled from the calendar (the Console omits days you did not use), the projection extends the last seven-day average to the reset, and `┊` marks the day the pace exhausts the monthly allowance — green before it, amber after. A real budget's cap is drawn as `╌`; Go has only per-model allowances, so no dollar cap is invented for it. **Colours.** A five-step pressure scale from theme tokens: green (< 30% used), grey (30–65%), yellow (65–85%), orange (a pace that exhausts the allowance before its reset, or 85–100%), red (rate-limited, exhausted, or under an hour left). ## Data sources | Purpose | Endpoint | | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Local token/cost accounting | server route `/api/experimental/session/stats` (`session.stats`) | | Billed totals | `GET https://opencode.ai/console/api/usage/summary?range=24h\|7d\|30d` | | Daily billed series | `GET …/api/usage/cost-by-day?range=30d&bucket=day` | | Per-model rows | `GET …/api/usage/models?range=…&pageSize=100&page=N` | | Go allowance | `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` | | Workspace budgets | `GET …/api/policies/current-budgets` | The Console routes are not documented and can change without notice; the plugin then hides the affected block and keeps showing the local one. There is no credits-balance endpoint — `/api/billing/account` returns only a credit limit, and the drawer routes answer 403 — so prepaid balance is not shown. ## Limits - The **per-session split is an estimate**: token counts are exact, the dollar split is the catalog's share of each category, scaled to what the turns recorded. The Console aggregates by day, model and user — never by session. - **Pace needs five minutes** of samples before it projects anything; until then you see the reset time. - **Cache-write tokens are zero on Go** (OpenAI-style caching does not charge writes). They only become interesting with providers that do, such as direct Anthropic. - **The billed block needs the workspace sign-in**, so a machine with only an API key shows the local block alone. - The type contract for the v2 TUI API is **vendored** in [`types/`](types) because that API is not on npm yet; `bun check` therefore checks against a mirror of `packages/plugin/src/tui`, not the published package. ### When to use something else - **Only want the Go percentages, nothing about money or cache?** [`opencode-go-usage`](https://github.com/ridho9/opencode-go-usage) and [`opencode-go-meter`](https://github.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-go-meter) are smaller and do exactly that; the latter also forecasts where the current pace lands. - **Want per-project reports rather than a live view?** `opencode stats --project . --models --cost` ships with OpenCode and prints the same local data as a shareable card. - **Not using Console or Go at all?** The local block still works, but the pace and billed halves will stay hidden. ## Checks One command runs everything that has to pass before a commit: ```bash bun install bun run gate ``` | Step | What it proves | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `format` | `bun fmt --check` — 120 columns, no semicolons | | `types` | `bun check` | | `language` | no German in tracked files (this repository is English only) | | `tests` | `bun test --coverage`, floors at 85% lines and 90% functions | | `aislop` | `WARN=ERR bun x aislop scan`, score 80 or better | | `gitleaks` | no secrets in the commit history | | `trufflehog` | no verified secrets in the commit history | `bun run verify` is the fast loop (types, format, language, tests). `bun run secrets:deep` additionally reports unverified secret candidates. The gate needs [`gitleaks`](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks#installing) and [`trufflehog`](https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog#installation) on `PATH`, and fails rather than skipping them. Tests cover what broke in practice: month arithmetic across month ends, calendar gaps versus the UTC day keys the Console uses, cap selection between budgets on different cycles, pace baselines across a window reset, credential fallback between database files, and malformed payloads. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the repository rules. ## License MIT
